# SEO-593: Include the primary content in the initial HTML response

This page is generated from the canonical JSONL registry record. Edit the JSONL record and run `npm run docs -- --write`; do not edit this file directly.

| --- | --- |

| Confidence | `HIGH` |

## Statement

The main content of each indexable route is present in the response body as delivered, before any client script runs, rather than fetched and inserted afterwards.

## Rationale

Any consumer that reads the response without executing script sees whatever the body contains at that moment, so a body holding only a mount point describes a page with no content regardless of what the browser later shows.

## Applicability

```json
{
  "all": [
    "public_site"
  ],
  "any": [
    "client_rendered",
    "javascript_app"
  ]
}
```

## Implementation

Move the route from a purely client-rendered mode into the framework's server-rendered or prerendered mode, fetching the data during the render rather than in an effect after mount. Where a route genuinely cannot render on the server, record that and do not present it as indexable.

## Verification

- Level: `SOURCE_AND_RUNTIME`
- Method: Fetch each route with script execution disabled and compare the visible text of the delivered body against the text present after hydration.
- Evidence: `RAW_HTML`, `RENDERED_HTML`, `ROUTE`
- Automated check: `content-in-initial-html`

## Scope

- Search surfaces: `GOOGLE_SEARCH`, `BING_SEARCH`, `AI_ASSISTANT_RETRIEVAL`
- Frameworks: `react-spa`, `vite`, `next-app-router`, `next-pages-router`, `astro`, `remix`, `sveltekit`, `nuxt`
